text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today, rebounding after a sharp five-day sell-off that had dropped the stock 6.97% since late October. The bounce comes as U.S. oil prices have held firm at $103 a barrel and refineries are running at a high 92.8% capacity—conditions that support strong margins for a refiner. The rebound also follows the company's leadership change announcement on October 29th and reported company update, which may have sparked renewed investor interest after the recent downturn.

The stock's recovery fits into a broader pattern this week: while Big Oil earnings are surging and refining margins have been historically strong (as fuel supplies remain tight), investors had grown cautious heading into earnings season on concerns about forward guidance. Today's move suggests some of that caution has eased, at least temporarily. The geopolitical backdrop—ongoing Iran-U.S. tensions—continues to support crude prices, though gasoline prices remain elevated despite Trump's campaign promise to lower them, which could weigh on refiner sentiment longer-term.
